svg.title: All accepted: pipeline fill and steady progress
svg.desc: Aligned recurrent steps, with S9–S12 and S14–S15 omitted in both panels. Both produce target results through x10; pipeline does so at S13 versus block S16.
svg.text: All accepted · from pipeline fill to steady progress
Target = 4 loops · draft = 1 loop · block K = 4. P = PRELUDE; C = CODA. Processing xi predicts the next token.
Columns align recurrent steps, NOT elapsed time. Both panels omit the same S9–S12 and S14–S15 intervals (⋯).
Compare the same GPU-ready outputs: green frames reach x5; purple frames reach x10. Younger speculative work can remain in flight.
After S8, start a new block at x5: 5 shallow steps (S9–S13), then R2–R4 verification (S14–S16).
S8 → S16: 8 more recurrent executions to produce x6–x10. The omitted columns contain work, not idle time.
After S8, x5 is already at R3, x6 at R2, x7 at R1. Each subsequent step can finish one more token when accepted.
S8 → S13: 5 more recurrent executions to produce x6–x10. This is 3 fewer executions (37.5%), not a measured latency percentage.
Each S counts one recurrent loop execution. PRELUDE, CODA, collection costs and different token-row counts still affect actual performance.
Only valid tokens and used P/C results are shown; inactive/padding rows and unused computations are omitted.
Async: copy-stream D2H and CPU collect occur later; GPU progress does not wait for CPU delivery.
